articles.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 | Propaganda for US war in Korea?
articles.author: Amanda Yee
articles.content_excerpt: The new Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 just dropped, and it’s already mired in controversy. The game simulates urban warfare in Seoul, casting players as a South Korean marine fighting off an invasion from the DPRK. Is this video game harmless entertainment, or is it sophisticated imperialist propaganda designed to “manufacture consent” for war against North Korea and normalize US militarism? Ju-Hyun Park, organizer with Nodutdol for Korean Community Development and director of engagement at Breakthrough News, joins Amanda Yee to break down the dangerous political messaging behind Modern Warfare 4.

articles.title: Keytruda was built on public science. Why does Merck own the rewards?
articles.author: David Franco
articles.content_excerpt: Keytruda is often presented as the ultimate success story of modern pharmaceutical innovation. And in one sense, that is true. Few medicines have transformed oncology as profoundly as pembrolizumab. It has extended survival in melanoma, lung cancer, and many other malignancies, and it has helped turn immune checkpoint inhibition from a scientific hypothesis into a clinical reality. For many patients, it has meant years of life that previously had few options at all. But that is only one part of the story. The other part is far less comfortable. articles.title: “Paraguay Is in Dire Need of Change”: Senator on Bank Collapse & Political Crisis
articles.content_excerpt: The collapse of Ueno Bank in Paraguay has plunged the country into crisis and led to the ouster of right-wing President Santiago Peña, a staunch ally of the Trump administration. At least 3 million people — nearly half of Paraguay’s population — lost access to their accounts on November 3 after regulators seized the insolvent bank amid allegations of widespread fraud. Peña, who had close ties to Ueno and appointed a former executive to lead Paraguay’s central bank, attempted to resign the presidency following the bank’s collapse. Lawmakers, however, rejected his resignation and impeached him instead, thereby stripping him of immunity from prosecution. He has since been placed under house arrest. articles.title: The Rule of Law Project: New Effort Launched to Probe Corruption & State Violence in U.S.
articles.content_excerpt: As Democrats prepare to take control of Congress in January, party leaders say they intend to hold Trump officials accountable with stepped-up hearings and investigations. The administration, however, has responded with threats to launch its own investigations into lawmakers for carrying out their oversight responsibilities. “The oversight function of Congress is well established by the founders. It’s a normal part of government. The separation of powers requires oversight,” says Brad Adams, co-founder of The Rule of Law Project, which seeks to provide outside accountability due to what he describes as the administration’s refusal to investigate “obvious cases of corruption.”
